$comment: First-party plugin registry (AGL-417). THE single place that maps plugin ids to packages, register entry points, and API path prefixes. `tools/scripts/generate-plugin-manifests.mjs` turns this into the per-app generated loader manifests — the only files allowed to reference @aglyn/plugins-* outside libs/plugins. `catalog` is the plugin's row on the workspace and site switchboards (label, description, release flag, what switching it off for a site stops, and what a published site loses); the generator compiles every row, in `order`, into libs/aglyn plugin-manager/first-party-plugins.generated.ts, so a new plugin is declared here and nowhere in core (AGL-3080). An entry with no `catalog` is not on the switchboard. `capabilities` are further switchboard ids the same bundle serves. register keys: site = canvas/site components (client barrel), console = ConsoleExtension (client barrel), tenantApi/consoleApi = API handlers (/server entry), declarations = the light registrations core reads before any surface loads (`/declarations`, both apps, client and server), serverDeclarations = the same for the server alone (`/declarations.server`, platform-event subscriptions), consoleServerDeclarations = the same for the CONSOLE's server alone (`/declarations.console-server`, never loaded or bundled by the tenant runtime: for registrations that open what only the console holds), subprocessors = the third-party recipients the plugin's code sends data to, and its other hosts and its uses of hosts declared elsewhere (`/subprocessors`, called by the generator rather than at runtime, and written into the console's subprocessors manifest as data for the subprocessor inventory), planEntitlements = what each plan includes of the plugin's own entitlement keys (`/plan-entitlements`, called by the generator rather than at runtime and compiled into the catalog file as data that core's PLAN_ENTITLEMENTS composes, because the pricing tables and the plan comparison read it without loading a plugin), videoEmbedProviders = the video hosts whose own player the plugin's Video element frames (`/video-embed-providers`, called by the generator and compiled into the catalog file as data, which the published page and the tenant's frame-src read without loading the plugin), tenantEmails = the emails a site sends its own customers through the plugin (`/tenant-emails`, called by the generator and compiled into the email lib's tenant email catalog as data, which the send path reads without loading the plugin). activityMutationPaths = the plugin's modules that create, transfer or destroy a durable customer object, which `tools/scripts/check-activity-coverage.mjs` holds to logging an activity entry like the platform's own. `alwaysOn` here is the LOADER's meaning — the bundle activates whatever ids `ensure()` is given, so it defeats the per-page narrowing in required-site-plugins.ts and belongs only to `mui`, which the canvas cannot render without. A plugin that merely may not be switched OFF says so with `alwaysOn` in FIRST_PARTY_PLUGINS instead. `modules` (AGL-3116) names the subpath a surface registers from when that surface's code must not ride with the package root's — each site surface has its own module, so a published page never loads a console registrar. `contributes` (AGL-3116, required) declares what the plugin adds and where, in the shape a marketplace manifest uses (core `plugin-contributions.ts`): `site.components` = the canvas component ids it registers, `site.features` = the site runtimes it mounts on every page of a site that switched it on, `console.slots` = the widget slots and panels it fills, `console.routes` / `console.orgRoutes` = the console routes it serves, `console.shell` = it draws a nav tab, a provider or a staff tab the shell renders on every screen. The loaders place a plugin by this declaration alone, so `apps/console/specs/plugin-contributions-declared.spec.ts` holds it to what the registrars actually register. `hostCollections` (AGL-3080) = the subcollections under a site the plugin owns (core `plugin-host-collections.ts`); a collection's `resource` is the KIND a client creates a document in it as, through the platform's generic create route — its field allow-list, plan counter, feature and stamps (core `plugin-host-resources.ts`), compiled and never registered, because that route is a security path. `sitemapSections` (AGL-3080) = the child sitemaps the plugin's own pages fill (core `plugin-sitemap-sections.ts`), compiled because the tenant's sitemap is a published-site reader. `taxReturnSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin sells through the platform's own account and registers a tax return source (core `plugin-tax-return-sources.ts`); the operator's sales tax return refuses to be filed while a declared source is unregistered. `revenueSource: true` (AGL-3080) = the plugin earns the operator a take through the platform's account and registers a revenue source (core `plugin-revenue-sources.ts`); the staff revenue report names a declared source it could not read rather than counting it as zero. `notificationCategories` (AGL-3080) = the preference buckets the plugin's notification types fall in, by the prefix before the dot: an `id` no other plugin and not the core owns, a `label` and `description` for the settings page, and `defaults` for the console and email channels; compiled into the catalog file and read by core `notifications.ts`, because the fan-out resolves channels in processes that load no plugin. The id keys stored preferences, so it is never renamed. `notificationDigests` (AGL-3080) = the digests the plugin sends on its own schedule: the `key` its on-by-default switch is stored under in `users/{uid}.digestPrefs`, and the switch's `label` and `description`, compiled the same way so the settings page draws it without loading the plugin.

catalog.label: Components
catalog.description: The base component and theme library every site builds on.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace and switchable per site (AGL-3029): the catalog and the submissions already stored belong to the workspace. A site's switch reaches every half of a form through this id, so no half keeps running behind a page that no longer shows it.
catalog.label: Forms
catalog.description: Forms on the site and the catalog that owns them.

siteOff.stops: Switching Forms off for this site stops forms rendering on its published pages, refuses every submission sent to it, and blocks publishing a form, or a page that carries one, until Forms is back on.
siteOff.keeps: Submissions already received, the workspace’s form catalog and the CRM leads its forms created are kept, and forms keep working on the workspace’s other sites.

pages.heading: These published pages carry a form. Their forms stop rendering and stop accepting submissions:
pages.none: No published page on this site carries a form.

catalog.label: Bookings
catalog.description: Services, open slots, and paid bookings.

resource.label: services
resource.$comment: `crmFollowUpTask` and `crmMeetingActivity` are the two CRM switches a service carries (AGL-2660): whether a booking files a meeting on the record, and whether it owes a follow-up task.

hostCollections.name: bookings
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Booking records — a customer, a time and a service pointer. The service holds the imagery and IS scanned; a booking is the transaction against it.

catalog.$comment: The Members blocks and the membership/* handlers are registered by this bundle, so there is no separate package to load; what this id contributes is the SWITCH the tenant route gate, the console card and the sitemap all ask (AGL-2486). Commerce off = member pages with no server, hence requires.
catalog.label: User Accounts
catalog.description: Visitor accounts on the site: the /signin, /signup and /recover pages, and the Members blocks. On for a new site; a site created before that stays off until you turn it on.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: User Accounts
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Visitor accounts on published sites: the /signin, /signup and /recover pages and the Members blocks (AGL-2486). Platform-wide kill switch only — whether a given SITE serves those pages is the per-site User Accounts toggle, which is off until a site opts in.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Commerce v2
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Full ecommerce wave: catalog/variants, cart + checkout, digital goods, reservations, POS, and the repriced commerce tiers (AGL-276..331).

resource.label: products
resource.$comment: The whole product model: the editor, the duplicate action and the CSV importer each send a full product. `nameLower`, `nameTokens`, `nameReversed`, `skus`, `barcodes`, `priceFromCents`, `soldOut` and `collectionIds` are the search, price, stock and smart-collection keys this plugin derives on the payload (`productSearchFields`, `productStockFields`, `productCollectionIds`; AGL-2501, AGL-3321), so they are allow-listed rather than stamped. `priceUsd`, `inventory` and `imageUrl` are the legacy Commerce Starter fields every caller still writes. Born live — `deletedAt: null` — because the products table queries `deletedAt == null` and Firestore cannot match an absent field; a duplicate never carries its source's soft delete.

hostCollections.name: siteMemberCredentials
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: A site member's password hash, one document per member, read and written only by the membership routes (AGL-3308). A credential with no content field, and no client may read it.

hostCollections.name: orders
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Completed orders. Line items COPY a product's `imageUrl` at purchase time, so these would match — and matching would be the wrong answer: an order is an immutable record of what was sold, deleting the asset changes nothing about it, and no author can edit one. A busy store also holds more of these than the whole read budget.

hostCollections.name: carts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Live and abandoned carts, with the same copied line-item image and the same reasoning, at higher volume — one document per shopper session.

hostCollections.name: checkouts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: In-flight checkout sessions. Transient buyer state carrying the same line-item snapshot as `carts`.

hostCollections.name: reservations
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS and booking holds. Short-lived transaction rows pointing at a resource that is itself scanned.

hostCollections.name: stockHolds
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Inventory holds taken during checkout. Machine-written, short-lived, and a quantity rather than content.

hostCollections.name: subscriptions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Site membership subscriptions: a plan pointer, a status and Stripe ids. Server-written from the billing webhook.

hostCollections.name: registers
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: POS register allocations — a count against the register add-on, read by billing (AGL-1775). No content field at all.

resource.label: POS registers
resource.$comment: The count is met against the site's allocation of the org's register seats (AGL-1775), which the platform resolves from this quota key; `pos` gates POS at all.

hostCollections.name: giftCards
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Gift card balances and redemption history. Money, not content.

hostCollections.name: licenseKeys
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Digital-product license keys issued at fulfilment: a code, an order pointer and a revocation flag.

hostCollections.name: inventoryAdjustments
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: The append-only stock adjustment ledger (AGL-2269). One row per manual stock edit and per cancellation release, unbounded over a store's life.

hostCollections.name: inventoryReconciliation
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Reconciliation runs comparing counted stock against recorded stock. Machine-written totals.

hostCollections.name: restockAlerts
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Back-in-stock requests: an email address and a product pointer, written by visitors.

hostCollections.name: stripeTaxRates
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Cached Stripe tax rate ids, written by the tax sync. Vendor ids.

sitemapSections.$comment: A product page for each active product with a slug, once the store names the template products render through (AGL-299). Soft deletes keep `status: active`, hence skipWhen. Commerce stamps epoch milliseconds.
The catalog collections served at /collections/{slug} (AGL-954), once the store names their template. A content collection is the platform's own section.

releaseFlagDefinition.$comment: navTabId (AGL-1654) is the marketplace plugin's own `orgNavItems` entry, held to a real declaration by `release-flag-nav-tab-ids.spec.ts`; the page behind it is gated (AGL-2019), so off means off.
releaseFlagDefinition.label: Marketplace
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Marketplace browsing, publishing and plugin installs.

notificationCategories.$comment: The id is persisted: every person's preferences for listing reviews are stored under `marketplace`, so it keeps this spelling.
notificationCategories.label: Marketplace
notificationCategories.description: Decisions on plugin listings you submitted for review.

catalog.$comment: The id was contacts until AGL-2595 widened one list into the hub; the release flag kept its key because it is persisted in Remote Config.
catalog.label: CRM
catalog.description: Leads, contacts, companies, deals, tasks and reports.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: CRM
releaseFlagDefinition.description: The CRM: contacts, leads, companies, deals, tasks, reports and fields.

hostCollections.name: leads
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Captured leads, on the same footing as `formSubmissions`: visitor-submitted, unbounded, and never a place an author places an asset.

notificationDigests.$comment: The key is persisted in every person's `digestPrefs`; the daily digest route reads the same one.
notificationDigests.label: Daily CRM digest
notificationDigests.description: Each morning: your overdue and due-today tasks and the leads nobody has worked, here and by email.

catalog.$comment: Works the CRM's records but is released and entitled on its own (AGL-2974). Reads Sequences since AGL-3199; the id is stored on every org, so it stays.
catalog.label: Sequences
catalog.description: One-to-one email sequences sent from connected mailboxes.

releaseFlagDefinition.$comment: The plugin's kill switch as well as its launch gate (AGL-2974). OFF by default, because nothing behind it sent mail at launch and no plan carries the `outreach` entitlement it also needs. The KEY stays `release_outreach`: it is persisted in Remote Config (AGL-3199).
releaseFlagDefinition.label: Sequences
releaseFlagDefinition.description: One-to-one, multi-step email sequences sent from a rep’s own connected mailbox and logged in the CRM (AGL-2974). OFF by default and staff preview only. An organization also needs the `outreach` entitlement, which no plan carries, so a customer reaches it only through a per-org entitlement override.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Data store
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Datasets, models and dynamic data bindings.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Email
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Designed emails, campaigns, and audience sending.

hostCollections.name: suppressions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Unsubscribes, bounces and spam complaints. Email addresses and a reason.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Inbox
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Form submissions, site members, and the lead inbox.

hostCollections.name: formSubmissions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: Visitor form submissions. Unbounded, PII-heavy, and a file attached to one is the visitor's upload — not a library asset an author picked, and not something deleting a library asset would break.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Logic
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Variables, no-code functions, and reference health.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Marketing
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Overlays, campaigns at-a-glance, and A/B experiments.

hostCollections.name: campaignAttributions
hostCollections.mediaScanReason: One row per conversion — a form submission, a lead, a contact or a booking — recording which campaign the visitor arrived from. Written only by the Admin SDK, and the whole record is three sanitized UTM strings capped at a hundred characters: there is no field an asset could occupy and no surface that could pick one into it. Unbounded on the same footing as the conversions it credits.

orgCollections.name: emailCampaigns
orgCollections.mediaScanReason: The campaign CONTAINER — a name, a date window, the list ids it is aimed at, a topic and the sites it runs on. Distinct from `campaigns`, which holds the sends and IS scanned because a send carries the copy that went out. A container carries no copy and no asset reference: the design a send renders is a screen, and the screen is where the picker writes.

resource.label: redirects
resource.$comment: A routing statement over the whole live site the moment it exists, not a draft (AGL-1881, AGL-2573): it needs the publishing role, an off-platform destination carries the uid of the publisher who chose it (the serve path refuses one without), and its source is announced to the site cache on create.

catalog.$comment: The id is stored on every org's enabled-plugin list; only the label moved.
catalog.label: Automation
catalog.description: Workflows, actions, webhooks, and run logs.

releaseFlagDefinition.label: Automation
releaseFlagDefinition.description: Workflows, actions, webhooks and their run history.

duplicate.$comment: The trigger is cleared, so a copy runs nothing until somebody arms it.

resource.label: webhooks
resource.$comment: Capped from a server read, never a client count (AGL-1360). `secret` stays client-supplied: it is generated with crypto.getRandomValues and the site's own editors read it off the card anyway.

resource.label: interactions and actions
resource.$comment: No entitlement (AGL-2266): the paid actions flag and the free interactions both write this collection, so the flag decides what RUNS, not what may be created. The full action model, because the actions card, the interaction builder and the preset wiring each send it.

orgCollections.name: automations
orgCollections.mediaScanReason: An org automation (AGL-3302) — a trigger, its conditions, the sites it is placed on, and a step list drawn from the server steps only: email subject and body as plain text, list, dataset and campaign ids, CRM fields and waits. No step it may hold carries a media reference, the in-page steps that could (custom HTML, popups) are refused by its save route, and it is written only by that route.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so, and no release flag (AGL-2939): the workspace half (the add-on, credits, allotments, overage billing, the staff doors) carries no site and must keep running whatever any one site decides. Its doors gate themselves one by one; a flag on the bundle would switch off the released doors with the unreleased ones.
catalog.label: AI
catalog.description: The assistant, generative building and automation, and the AI add-on.

siteOff.stops: Switching AI off for this site hides the assistant, Describe it, the AI cards and the editor’s AI controls on this site, refuses every AI request made for it, and stops its queued AI jobs without spending credits.
siteOff.keeps: It does not stop the workspace’s AI add-on, credits, allotments or overage billing, and AI keeps working on the workspace’s other sites.

catalog.$comment: On for every workspace, off for a site only when that site says so (AGL-3405): the built-in themes cost nothing until the theme page lists them, and a site that picked one keeps it whatever this switch says, because picking a theme copies it onto the site.
catalog.label: Themes
catalog.description: Built-in themes to pick from on Setup → Theme: Bootstrap, Minimal and Material 3.

siteOff.stops: Switching Themes off for this site removes its built-in themes from the theme picker.
siteOff.keeps: A site already using one keeps it, with every edit made to it: picking a theme copies it onto the site, so nothing on the published site changes.
